pages.notes: FBI form FD-245 with heavy redactions and FOIA markings; OCR predominantly captured marks and redacted areas as garbled text rather than the limited readable content (letterhead, form labels, document metadata).
OCR correctly captured the main typewritten interview reference and document IDs, but missed the handwritten classification/envelope notes at the bottom of the page.

Page contains heavily annotated handwritten text and official stamps on a faded photocopy; OCR captured footer information (NW 90290, DocId, Page 3) with reasonable accuracy but produced mostly garbled results for handwritten content and upper document sections.

Handwritten sketch page with annotated UFO sighting diagrams; OCR only captured footer metadata (NW 90290, DocId), completely missed handwritten notes, diagram labels, and sketch annotations due to cursive script and photocopy degradation.

Heavily faded form page with multiple redaction stamps/seals obscuring content; only the handwritten annotation at bottom (WLADYSLAW KRASUSKI, date, reference number) is legible, but OCR corrupted it significantly; most typewritten text above is illegible.
Handwritten name 'Franciszek Grabowski' at top was completely missed by OCR; only machine-printed footer text was captured from this aged form.

FBI form FD-125 with typewritten structure and handwritten entries (names, addresses); OCR correctly captures most field labels but severely mangles checkbox symbols as letters, misses or garbles handwritten text, and hallucinates entire lines of non-existent content.

FBI memo with clear typewritten text but OCR struggled with degraded areas; key errors include 'KIASUSKI' misread as 'KTASUSKI'/'cinsyeer', 'ELEVEN' as 'EKEVE N', 'TO KNOW' as 'me KNOW', and handwritten marks rendered as garbage characters.

FBI interview document with clear typewritten text and FOIA stamps. Main OCR error: 'Robert Gutler' should be 'Robert Cutler'. Redacted sections (FOIA markings) created garbled output. Overall text capture is strong despite age-related degradation.

Aged typewritten document with heavy OCR corruption; key terms like 'swamp area' rendered as 'wap area', 'cutting' as 'atting', and numerous character/word errors throughout. Overall structure preserved but individual word accuracy severely compromised by paper age, typewriter inconsistencies, and scan degradation.
OCR completely missed the main FBI distribution notice text at the top and only captured footer metadata; light faded scan likely caused the miss of the primary content.

FBI document with multiple OCR errors including consistent misreading of KRASUSKI as KHASUSKI/KiASUSKI, FROM→PROM, DETROIT→DETRUIT, address 2457→54.57, and garbled credit inquiry text; main content structure preserved but with character-level substitutions and number errors.

FBI memo on UAP observations from 1957; OCR captured main content structure but contains numerous spelling errors (DMTROIT/DETROIT, UNIDENTIFIAD/UNIDENTIFIED, REBUTEL/REBUTTAL, POURTY/FORTY, SLUWLY/SLOWLY) and character corruption (SU*®PICIENT, PO\W, UBSTRUCTED, siVeHAL), with some handwritten signatures and redaction marks present.
1966 letter from Oklahoma UFO Research Association to FBI; typewritten body text captured accurately but organizational letterhead missing and handwritten stamps/marks garbled in OCR.

Full FBI letter from 1986 addressed to Kerry Liesch regarding UFO research; OCR captured only footer metadata (NW 90290, DocId) correctly while severely garbling the recipient name, organization, and sender information.
